protocol.name: sherlock_shell_v1

description.summary: windows and screens for the programs of the shell

protocol.description:
Private protocol between the compositor and the programs of the shell: the bar, the dock, and later Sherlock's window server. It lists the windows with their states and geometry, acts on them, and tells for each screen whether a maximized or fullscreen window is on it. Workspaces go through the standard ext-workspace-v1 protocol, offered on the same terms: its list, its active workspace and its activate request. This protocol adds what ext-workspace-v1 does not carry: the workspace of each window, and moving a window to another workspace. A workspace is named here by the id that ext_workspace_handle_v1 gives it (its id event).
The compositor only offers the globals of this protocol to clients that connected through the shell socket: the Wayland socket of the session followed by "-shell", in the same directory (wayland-1-shell for wayland-1). Clients of the ordinary socket, XWayland and the sandboxed applications that only see that socket never see the global, and cannot bind it. See ADR 0021.
Screens are named by their wl_output name (wl_output version 4, or xdg-output): the shell programs usually talk to this protocol on a connection of their own, where the wl_output objects of their surfaces do not exist. Rectangles are in logical pixels, relative to the top left corner of the named screen.
Versioning: a backward compatible change adds requests, events or enum entries and bumps the interface version. An incompatible change renames the interfaces with a new suffix (sherlock_shell_manager_v2) and the protocol (sherlock_shell_v2). A toplevel object has the version of the manager that announced it.
Version 2 adds the snapped value of output_state. Version 4 adds show_windows, for App Expose. Version 3 is taken by the global menu (lot D-36).

interface.name: sherlock_shell_manager_v1

description.summary: list of the windows and state of the screens

interface.description: Once bound, the compositor sends a toplevel event for every window that shows content, with its properties, then an output event for every screen, then done. After that, it sends the changes as they happen: new windows, changed properties, closed windows, changed screens, each batch ended by done. A client applies what it received at done.

request.name: destroy
request.description: The compositor sends nothing more on this manager nor on its toplevels. The toplevel objects stay valid until the client destroys them, and their requests still act.

event.name: toplevel
event.description: A window shows content, or was already there when the manager was bound. Its id, title, app_id, state, output, workspace and geometry follow, before the next done.

entry.name: maximized
entry.summary: a maximized window, not minimized, is on the screen

entry.name: fullscreen
entry.summary: a fullscreen window, not minimized, is on the screen

entry.name: snapped
entry.summary: a window snapped to a half or a quarter, not minimized, is on the screen

event.name: output

description.summary: a screen and what covers it

event.description: Sent for each screen when the manager is bound, then when the state of a screen changes or a screen appears. A window is on the screen under its center. Only the windows of the active workspace count. The state is an array of 32-bit values of output_state, in the machine's byte order; an empty array means no maximized, fullscreen nor snapped window is on it. The snapped value is only sent to a manager bound at version 2 or later.

event.name: output_removed
event.description: The screen of this name is gone. The windows that were on it move to another screen in the same batch.

request.name: show_windows

description.summary: Mission Control on some windows: App Expose

request.description: Opens Mission Control with only these windows, by the ids of their id events: the windows of one application, as the dock groups them (a Wayland app_id and an X11 class may both belong to it). Mission Control shows those of them that it would show, the windows of the active workspace that are not minimized, without the strip of the workspaces, and behaves as usual: a click on a window chooses it, a click elsewhere or Escape closes the view. Unknown ids are ignored; when no window is left to show, the request does nothing. While Mission Control is already open, it shows these windows instead.

arg.name: windows
arg.summary: window ids, 32-bit values in the machine's byte order

event.name: done

description.summary: end of a batch of changes

event.description: Every event since the previous done (or since the bind) forms one consistent state of the windows and the screens.

interface.name: sherlock_shell_toplevel_v1
interface.description: One window, Wayland or X11. Its events come in any order between two done events of the manager. The id comes first, once. A window on a workspace that is not active keeps its states; it is simply not shown.

entry.name: invalid_rectangle
entry.summary: width or height is negative, or x + width or y + height overflows a 32-bit signed integer

request.name: destroy
request.description: The client no longer receives events about this window. The window itself stays.

request.name: activate
request.description: Brings the window back if it is minimized, raises it and gives it the keyboard, unless an anchored surface keeps the keyboard for itself.

request.name: minimize
request.description: Hides the window until it is activated. The window that is then on top becomes the active one.

request.name: close
request.description: The application receives the close request of its toolkit (xdg_toplevel.close, or WM_DELETE_WINDOW for X11), and may ask the user first.

request.name: move_to_workspace

description.summary: put the window on another workspace

request.description: The window leaves its workspace for the one of this id (the id event of ext_workspace_handle_v1). An unknown id is ignored.

request.name: set_rectangle

description.summary: where the window goes when minimized

request.description: The rectangle of the dock icon that stands for this window, kept by the compositor for the minimize animation. A width or height of 0 removes it. It replaces the previous one, and goes with the window, not with the client. A negative width or height, or a rectangle whose x + width or y + height does not fit in a 32-bit signed integer, is the invalid_rectangle error.

event.name: id
event.description: Identifies the window for as long as it exists, and is never given to another window while the compositor runs. Every client receives the same id for the same window.

event.name: app_id
event.description: The xdg-shell app_id, or the class of an X11 window. Empty when the client gave none.

entry.name: snapped
entry.summary: placed in a half or a quarter of its screen

entry.name: activated
entry.summary: the active window, the last one given the keyboard

event.name: state
event.description: Array of 32-bit values of the state enum, in the machine's byte order. The active window keeps its state while an anchored surface (the bar, the dock) has the keyboard.

event.name: output
event.description: The screen under the center of the window. A minimized window keeps the one it had.

event.name: workspace
event.description: The id of the workspace the window belongs to, as the id event of ext_workspace_handle_v1 gives it. A window belongs to one workspace.

event.name: geometry

description.summary: place and size of the window

event.description: Relative to the screen given by the output event, in logical pixels, without the shadow. The target of an animation, not each step of it. A minimized window keeps the geometry it had.

event.name: closed
event.description: The window no longer exists. No more events come on this object, whose requests do nothing; the client should destroy it.
